slides.title: Argument Passing Semantics
slides.prompt: C++ supports Pass-by-Value (makes a copy), Pass-by-Reference (creates an alias to the original variable), and Pass-by-Pointer (passes memory address explicitly).
slides.codeSnippet:
void byVal(int x) { x = 10; }       // No change to original
void byRef(int& x) { x = 10; }      // Modifies original
void byPtr(int* x) { if(x) *x=10; } // Modifies original via pointer

slides.title: Pass-by-Reference Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the reference operator to enable modifying the original argument.

slides.title: Performance Benefit of Const References
slides.prompt: Why use 'const std::string&' as a function parameter instead of 'std::string'?
options: To prevent expensive deep copies while ensuring the caller data remains unmodified
To force the function to return a value faster
To allocate the parameter on the heap
slides.correctAnswer: To prevent expensive deep copies while ensuring the caller data remains unmodified

slides.title: Pass-by-Pointer Dereferencing
slides.prompt: Fill in the dereference operator to update the value at the passed address.

slides.title: Nullability Difference
slides.prompt: What is a primary advantage of Pass-by-Pointer over Pass-by-Reference?
options: Pointers can be nullptr, allowing optional argument passing
Pointers are faster to access than references
References cannot be used with custom classes
slides.correctAnswer: Pointers can be nullptr, allowing optional argument passing

slides.title: Const Reference Parameter
slides.prompt: Fill in the const keyword to make a read-only reference parameter.

slides.title: Pass-by-Value Copy Effect
slides.prompt: What happens when a large object like std::vector<int> with 1 million items is passed by value?
options: All 1 million elements are copied to a new memory block, causing heavy overhead
Only the vector header is copied; elements remain shared
The compiler automatically converts it to a pointer
It results in a compile-time error
slides.correctAnswer: All 1 million elements are copied to a new memory block, causing heavy overhead

slides.title: Calling Pass-by-Pointer Function
slides.prompt: Fill in the address-of operator to pass a local variable to a pointer parameter.

slides.title: Modifying Pointer Arguments
slides.prompt: How do you allow a function to modify a pointer address itself (e.g., reallocate memory)?
options: Pass a pointer reference (T*&) or double pointer (T**)
slides.correctAnswer: Pass a pointer reference (T*&) or double pointer (T**)
